done_when: The first screen's Needs you count and list include every part or fix with failed checks idle for a day or more, each with a plain reason such as "checks failed, no activity for 7 days".

known.title: Not done: Needs you includes every part or fix with failed checks idle for a day or more
Do not report an idle failure while its checks are running
Keep the item detail's Needs you status consistent with the list

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. Case: normal use - an old pull request reruns a 120-job CI matrix, with a failure among the first 100 checks and a later job still running. GitHub permits [up to 256 matrix jobs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax). `board_facts.py:75` requests only the first 100 contexts, `board.py:146-148` reports failure even when `hasNextPage` is true, and `board.py:571` looks for running checks only in that first page. The item is therefore still added to Needs you while a check runs, contrary to the owner's ruling.
findings.title: Do not report an idle failure while its checks are running

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - a manager opens the overflow list for five failed fixes. The revised test counts five generic Fix buttons and five identical reason strings, but never checks that they represent five distinct fixes. A renderer that repeats the first fix five times would pass while the other four remain unreachable. All five fixtures also belong to the viewer, so the Me assertions pass if Needs you incorrectly shows the unfiltered Team list.
findings.title: Gate: test_2_five_idle_failed_fixes_fit_the_first_screen

stop.reason: The owner chose: repair the test only; the more-than-100-checks edge is an accepted known issue

why: A part or fix with failed checks and no activity for a day or more sits under Building, so a manager reads "0 need you" and thinks nothing needs doing.
